samples.summary: No test covers the actual production wiring (`data-canvas-toolbar` + hook) on SlidesToolbar or BoardToolbar
samples.evidence: The new test file only mounts a hand-written `<div data-canvas-toolbar="">` harness (toolbar-focus-release.test.tsx:22-53). Nothing asserts that the real `SlidesToolbar` (index.tsx:110) or `BoardToolbar` (board-toolbar.tsx:186) renders the opt-in attribute or calls `useCanvasFocusRelease()`. If either mount regressed (attribute dropped, hook removed, `Toolbar` stopping its `{...props}` spread at ui/toolbar.tsx:22), every test in the suite still passes and issue #882 silently returns. The whole production surface of this diff is untested; only the hook in isolation is.

samples.summary: The two Radix-dropdown tests (Escape close, menu-item select) may pass vacuously if focus lands on body naturally
samples.evidence: `expectFocusReleased()` only asserts `document.activeElement === document.body`. In jsdom, when a Radix `DropdownMenuContent` portal unmounts, focus can end up on `document.body` regardless of the hook (Radix's focus-restore-to-trigger relies on layout/focus behaviour that jsdom emulates imperfectly). If so, tests at lines 95-108 — the ones that model the actual #882 repro (Radix hands focus back to the trigger) — would stay green with `useCanvasFocusRelease()` deleted, i.e. fake coverage of the central scenario. A stronger form would first assert `document.activeElement === trigger` after close with the hook disabled, or assert the trigger was blurred (e.g. spy/`toHaveFocus` on the trigger before the deferred tick).

The "Text color" harness button carries BOTH `aria-expanded="true"` and `data-state="open"` (lines 37-39), so the test at line 67 passes if either half of the `hasOpenPopup()` condition (toolbar-focus-release.ts:64-69) is removed. Neither the aria-expanded-only nor the data-state-only case is covered, and the guard is also never verified against a REAL open Radix dropdown trigger (the `Arrange` menu is only checked after it closes) — so 'opening a menu still works' is not asserted.

samples.summary: `POPUP_SELECTOR` non-menu branches and the pointer-outside-toolbar case are untested
samples.evidence: Only `role="menu"` is exercised (via the DropdownMenu). No test drives a `role="dialog"`, `role="listbox"` or `[data-radix-popper-content-wrapper]` surface (POPUP_SELECTOR, toolbar-focus-release.ts:57-58), and no test asserts the negative case in `isPointerDrivenTarget` — a pointerdown OUTSIDE the toolbar/popup followed by a toolbar focusin must NOT release focus. Those branches can break undetected.

samples.summary: Cleanup path (listener removal / pending timeout clear on unmount) has no test
samples.evidence: The effect's teardown at toolbar-focus-release.ts:123-129 clears the pending timeout and removes three capture listeners; no test unmounts the harness and then dispatches pointerdown/focusin to prove no stray blur happens after unmount (a leaked release could blur an unrelated app element). Searched the whole new test file and packages/frontend/tests for any unmount-based case for this hook.

samples.summary: Keepalive test marks the button itself, not an ancestor wrapper as production does
samples.evidence: Production puts `data-text-edit-keepalive` on wrapper divs / DropdownMenuContent (e.g. font-size-picker.tsx:145, text-format-group.tsx:245), whereas the test at line 48 puts it directly on the button. Since `isReleasable` uses `closest()`, the ancestor-wrapper shape (the one that actually ships) is never exercised.

verdict.reason: The wiring is real in production code (slides/toolbar/index.tsx:4,70,110 and board/board-toolbar.tsx:5,137,186) and nothing tests it. Grep over all test files for SlidesToolbar/BoardToolbar/board-toolbar/toolbar-index yields only MobileSlidesToolbar (mobile-text-toggles.test.ts:24) and a comment in is-editable-target.test.ts:50; no test imports components/ui/toolbar, so the `{...props}` spread that carries data-canvas-toolbar (ui/toolbar.tsx:22) is unasserted. Repo-wide grep for data-canvas-toolbar/CANVAS_TOOLBAR_ATTR/useCanvasFocusRelease finds only the hook, its own isolated unit test, the two toolbars, and docs. Indirect routes checked and ruled out: no frontend e2e/spec files exist; .trusted/scripts/agent/hunt-ui.test.mjs parses board-toolbar.tsx source but only for BoardToolbarProps callbacks and control names (no `focus` match); harness/visual/slides-scenarios.tsx renders SlidesToolbar only for pixel baselines, which cannot detect a missing attribute or hook call; tests/components/menu-focus.test.ts covers the older releaseFocusToBody/useMenuCloseHandlers palette helpers, not this hook. The hook's own test is meaningful but drives a hand-written harness (toolbar-focus-release.test.tsx:22-53), so a regression at either mount point leaves the suite green and issue #882 silently returns — a changed behavior with no meaningful test, in-lane and blocking.

verdict.reason: The quoted evidence checks out: expectFocusReleased() asserts only document.activeElement === document.body via a polling waitFor, and the two Radix tests (Escape at 95-101, menu-item select at 103-108) rely on nothing stronger. The dropdown is real Radix (ui/dropdown-menu.tsx wraps @radix-ui/react-dropdown-menu). Both Radix's focus-restore-to-trigger and the hook's release (toolbar-focus-release.ts:119-122) are deferred by 0ms timers, so there is a window after the portal unmounts where activeElement falls back to body with no help from the hook, and a polling waitFor can pass on that window. I could not rule this out: node_modules/@radix-ui is not installed so I could not read onCloseAutoFocus, no other test in the repo pins Radix's focus-to-trigger behaviour under this jsdom/userEvent setup (menu-focus.test.ts tests the helper in isolation, font-family-picker.test.ts asserts DOM teardown, arrange-menu.test.tsx makes no focus assertions), and I cannot execute the suite. The plain-button (61-65) and toggle (77-83) tests do give real coverage of the general release path, but the Radix trigger-refocus / POPUP_SELECTOR path — which the module comment calls the actual #882 failure mode — is covered only by these two possibly non-discriminating assertions. No refutation ground applies: the code is present as described, reachable, and vacuous coverage of a changed behaviour is squarely in this lens.
